periods.analysis: We are yellow overall, and I read that as unfinished work, not failure. The Federal Graduation Rate is a solid green at 91.6%, above the >=90 target, which tells me our senior on-track systems are doing their job. The harder truth is in the early and next-step indicators: 3rd-Grade Reading Proficiency is 57.4% against a >=65 target, and College & Career Readiness is 54.1% against a >=60 target. At the school level, the watch-item is chronic absenteeism among K-3 students on the East Harbor and Bayside feeder routes, where missed Mondays and post-holiday absences are cutting into reading minutes.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green graduation result by keeping the Senior Success Team on every student with fewer than 18 credits or any failed core course, with weekly counselor reviews through PowerSchool cohort list S24-ONTRACK. Extend the Harborview Reads tutoring block to the six lowest-performing 3rd-grade classrooms at Lincoln, Mariner, and Seaport Elementary, using trained City Library reading corps volunteers four mornings per week. For readiness, add a fall FAFSA, dual-enrollment, and industry credential push through the Airport-Seaport Career Pathways cohort, with named caseload owners for each senior not yet meeting a readiness marker.

periods.analysis: The overall status remains yellow, and this quarter moved the wrong way in all three measures. Graduation stayed green but slipped from 91.6% to 91.3%, a 0.3-point decline that is small but worth watching before midyear course failures harden. 3rd-Grade Reading Proficiency fell from 57.4% to 56.0%, down 1.4 points, and College & Career Readiness moved from 54.1% to 53.3%, down 0.8 points. I am most concerned about the reading dip because winter absenteeism and substitute coverage gaps at three coastal-zone schools reduced the consistency of the 90-minute literacy block.
periods.recommendations: Protect the graduation green by running a January credit-recovery sweep for all seniors with one or two missing credits, using evening seats at Harborview High and Southport Academy. Treat the 56.0% reading result as the watch-item: deploy literacy coaches to observe and reset small-group instruction in the 18 classrooms flagged by the December benchmark. Rebuild readiness momentum by opening 120 additional spring seats in dual enrollment and maritime logistics credentials, and require counselors to contact every senior missing only one readiness indicator.

periods.analysis: We are still yellow, but the quarter shows the first signs of a disciplined correction. Graduation held flat at 91.3%, remaining green and above the >=90 target, which is exactly the kind of stability we need while we work on earlier grades. 3rd-Grade Reading Proficiency improved from 56.0% to 57.3%, up 1.3 points, and College & Career Readiness increased from 53.3% to 53.7%, up 0.4 points. The watch-item is whether the reading gain is broad-based or concentrated in a few classrooms that received coach support first.
periods.recommendations: Sustain graduation by continuing Friday senior check-ins for attendance, credits, and postsecondary plans, with principals reviewing the same 91.3% cohort every week until graduation. Scale the reading practices that produced the 1.3-point gain by moving the Mariner Elementary phonics walk-through protocol to all K-3 campuses by March 15. For readiness, create a counselor dashboard showing students within one action of qualifying through SAT/ACT, CTE credential, AP, IB, dual enrollment, or military enlistment evidence.

periods.analysis: The yellow rating remains appropriate, but this is the second consecutive quarter of movement in the right direction on the two lagging measures. Graduation eased from 91.3% to 91.2%, down 0.1 point, yet it remains green and safely above the >=90 target. 3rd-Grade Reading Proficiency rose from 57.3% to 58.0%, up 0.7 points, and College & Career Readiness rose from 53.7% to 54.2%, up 0.5 points. The watch-item now shifts to summer learning loss, especially for readers who just crossed benchmark but remain fragile.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the graduation green by enrolling off-track juniors and rising seniors in June credit recovery before they leave campus, not after they disappear in July. Extend Harborview Reads into a six-week Summer Literacy Bridge at Lincoln, Seaport, and Bayview, prioritizing the 312 students within five scale-score points of proficiency. Keep readiness climbing by reserving summer credential labs at the Port Training Center for OSHA-10, ServSafe, and logistics fundamentals, with transportation from the Route 7 and Route 12 school hubs.

periods.analysis: We remain yellow, and the mixed movement tells me we have not yet made the system reliable enough. Graduation improved from 91.2% to 91.8%, up 0.6 points and still green, which reflects strong summer completion work and senior re-engagement. 3rd-Grade Reading Proficiency fell from 58.0% to 56.8%, down 1.2 points, while College & Career Readiness held flat at 54.2%. The watch-item is the transition back from summer: several schools opened with teacher vacancies in primary grades, and the first 20 instructional days matter too much to lose.
periods.recommendations: Sustain and extend the graduation gain by converting the summer re-engagement playbook into a standing September attendance-and-credit protocol for every high school. Address the reading setback by assigning the district's strongest literacy coaches to vacancy-affected K-3 teams for daily lesson internalization and Friday data meetings through the first nine weeks. For readiness, unstick the flat 54.2% by pre-registering seniors for fall SAT school day, CTE credential exams, and dual-enrollment courses before the October add-drop window closes.

periods.analysis: The yellow status is still the honest status, and this quarter is a reminder that graduation strength cannot mask earlier pipeline weakness. Graduation declined from 91.8% to 91.0%, down 0.8 points, but remains green and above the >=90 target. 3rd-Grade Reading Proficiency edged down from 56.8% to 56.6%, a 0.2-point decline, and College & Career Readiness dropped from 54.2% to 53.7%, down 0.5 points. My watch-item is chronic absenteeism after the November tidal-flooding closures, which hit families in the Shoreline Terrace and Canal District attendance zones and disrupted both reading intervention and credential testing.
periods.recommendations: Keep graduation green by immediately reviewing every senior affected by the 0.8-point decline, with make-up seat time and credit-recovery plans assigned before winter break. Launch a flood-disruption recovery schedule at Shoreline Terrace, Canal View, and Bayfront Elementary, adding two 30-minute reading intervention blocks per week for students who missed three or more days. Recover readiness by offering December and January make-up testing windows and weekend credential labs, with city transit passes issued to students from the impacted zones.

periods.analysis: We are yellow overall, but the quarter shows a constructive rebound after the Q4 softness. Graduation increased from 91.0% to 91.9%, up 0.9 points and still green, which is a credit to the counselors, attendance liaisons, and families who stayed close to the senior list. 3rd-Grade Reading Proficiency rose from 56.6% to 56.9%, up 0.3 points, and College & Career Readiness rose from 53.7% to 54.1%, up 0.4 points. The watch-item is pace: these gains are real, but they are not yet fast enough to close the gap to 65% reading proficiency or 60% readiness.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 91.9% graduation performance by keeping the winter senior audit active through spring, including weekly checks on attendance, credits, and required assessments. Accelerate reading by moving from broad intervention to student-specific skill groups, using the January i-Ready strand report to place every below-benchmark 3rd grader into phonics, fluency, vocabulary, or comprehension groups. Push readiness by giving each high school a named target list of seniors within one credential, assessment score, or dual-enrollment completion of meeting the readiness standard.

periods.analysis: The year closes still yellow, but with the strongest combined improvement in the two yellow measures since this arc began. Graduation moved from 91.9% to 91.5%, down 0.4 points, yet remains green and above the >=90 target; we should not take that for granted, but it is durable. 3rd-Grade Reading Proficiency increased from 56.9% to 57.9%, up 1.0 point, and College & Career Readiness improved from 54.1% to 55.3%, up 1.2 points. The watch-item is sustaining that late-year readiness lift without letting summer absenteeism and mobility undo the reading progress for rising 4th graders.
periods.recommendations: Protect the green graduation result by locking in senior transition conferences before students leave for summer, especially for rising seniors with attendance below 90%. Extend the reading rebound through a Rising 4th Grade Literacy Passport, with library check-ins, text-level goals, and targeted summer tutoring for students still below proficiency. Build on the 55.3% readiness result by renewing the Airport-Seaport Career Pathways slots, expanding credential testing before September, and assigning counselors to verify every readiness artifact in the student information system.

periods.analysis: Graduation remains above target at 91.2%, while reading improved to 58.4% and college and career readiness improved to 56.1%. Both improving measures remain below their targets, so the combined result is caution rather than a completed turnaround.
periods.recommendations: Protect graduation verification and use the FAST review and counselor record checks to focus the next cycle on students still short of proficiency or readiness.
